_comment: Inputs for /2027-tax-brackets/ and /2027-social-security-cola/. REFRESH after each BLS CPI release (2026-08-12 for reference month July 2026, 2026-09-11 for August 2026, 2026-10-14 for September 2026). REPLACE the projected-brackets page once the IRS Revenue Procedure for tax year 2027 lands (expected late October 2026) and replace the COLA figure once SSA announces (expected mid-October 2026). A month that BLS has not published is the literal null with a `due` date beside it in `schedule`: never interpolate it, never carry the previous month forward, never 'estimate the remaining months'.

ccpiu._what: Chained CPI for All Urban Consumers (C-CPI-U), U.S. city average, all items, not seasonally adjusted. BLS series SUUR0000SA0. This is the index 26 U.S.C. 1(f)(6) uses to index federal tax figures, after the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (P.L. 115-97) replaced CPI-U with it.
ccpiu._vintageNote: BLS issues C-CPI-U first as `initial`, revises it to `interim`, then finalises it roughly a year later as `final`. The vintage on each month below is the footnote BLS attached to that value on the date we retrieved it. Values without an initial/interim footnote are final.

2025-10.note: Never published. Data collection for October 2025 did not happen during the 2025 lapse in appropriations, and BLS has said it cannot collect those prices retroactively, so no October 2025 index exists and none is expected. The BLS series itself returns the footnote "Data unavailable due to the 2025 lapse in appropriations" for this month.

2026-07.note: July 2026 Consumer Price Index news release.

2026-08.note: August 2026 Consumer Price Index news release. This is the last month of the statutory window for tax year 2027.

cpiw._what: CPI for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W), U.S. city average, all items, not seasonally adjusted. BLS series CWUR0000SA0. This is the index the Social Security cost-of-living adjustment is computed from, comparing the third-quarter average of one year with the third-quarter average of the last year a COLA was set.

2026-07.note: July 2026 Consumer Price Index news release.

2026-08.note: August 2026 Consumer Price Index news release.

2026-09.note: September 2026 Consumer Price Index news release. The Social Security Administration normally announces the official COLA the same morning this release lands.

thirdPartyEstimates.title: COLA prediction remains high at 3.8% as Social Security falls behind cost of living
thirdPartyEstimates.note: TSCL's monthly model. Unchanged from its June 2026 reading and down from 3.9% in April 2026. Retrieved 2026-08-11; the page itself carries no publication date, the 2026-07-14 date is the monthly update TSCL describes.

thirdPartyEstimates.publisher: Mary Johnson (independent Social Security and Medicare policy analyst)
thirdPartyEstimates.title: Social Security COLA in 2027: Cooling inflation lowers estimate
thirdPartyEstimates.note: Revised down a full point from the 4.7% she published in June 2026 after the June CPI report. Anyone still quoting 4.7% is quoting the June figure.

base2026._note: The official tax-year-2026 figures a 2027 projection would be indexed from are NOT copied here. They live once, in src/data/tax-data-2026.json, which is the file the paycheck engine and every other tax page on this site already computes from. Duplicating them into this file would create two copies that can silently disagree. Recorded here is only the provenance of that file's federal block.

ccpiuDefinition.quote: the value of the C-CPI-U for any calendar year is the average of the C-CPI-U as of the close of the 12-month period ending on August 31 of such calendar year.

cumulativeBase.quote: The cost-of-living adjustment for any calendar year is the percentage (if any) by which the C-CPI-U for the preceding calendar year exceeds the CPI for calendar year 2016, multiplied by the amount determined under subparagraph (B).

roundingBrackets.quote: If any increase determined under paragraph (2)(A), section 63(c)(4), section 68(b)(2), or section 151(d)(4) is not a multiple of $50, such increase shall be rounded to the next lowest multiple of $50.

roundingMfs.quote: In the case of a married individual filing a separate return, subparagraph (A) (other than with respect to sections 63(c)(4) and 151(d)(4)(A)) shall be applied by substituting "$25" for "$50" each place it appears.

roundingStandardDeduction.cite: 26 U.S.C. § 63(c)(7)(B)(ii), as amended by P.L. 119-21 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act)
roundingStandardDeduction.quote: If any increase under this clause is not a multiple of $50, such increase shall be rounded to the next lowest multiple of $50.

thirdPartyProjections._note: Projected 2027 federal bracket figures published by a named, checkable publisher. Empty as of 2026-08-11: Bloomberg Tax, Thomson Reuters and Wolters Kluwer all publish their first-look projections in September, after the August CPI release completes the statutory window, and none had published for tax year 2027 when this file was written. Machine-generated calculator sites are already ranking with 2027 figures; they are deliberately not listed, because none of them state a window, a month list, or a source.
